As of **July 18, 2026**, the clean answer is:

You can have **one universal Codex CLI authentication** across your terminal, ACLI, and future systems, but only for the parts that use the **real `codex` CLI**. That shared auth is the Codex login cache, typically `~/.codex/auth.json`, not an API key. OpenAI’s current Codex docs say the CLI can sign in with ChatGPT, supports `codex login`, `codex login --device-auth`, and copying `~/.codex/auth.json` to headless machines or containers; they also say **API keys are still the recommended default for automation**. See [Codex CLI](https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli) and [Authentication](https://developers.openai.com/codex/auth).

Your current systems are split:

- ACLI’s Codex path already looks compatible with shared CLI auth. The adapter in [src/acli/adapters/codex.py](/Users/ed/King/clawd_2/development_channel/src/acli/adapters/codex.py) just runs `codex`; it does not inject a separate OpenAI key, so it will use whatever Codex auth the environment/home directory already has.

Its app path still uses `OPENAI_API_KEY` in [app/main.py](/Users/ed/King/clawd_2/voice_channel/app/main.py), and its worker registry maps `"codex"` to an `agy` adapter plus `CODEX_API_KEY` in [workers/registry.json](/Users/ed/King/clawd_2/voice_channel/workers/registry.json). That is not the same thing as reusing logged-in Codex CLI credentials.

So the safest architecture, without touching ACLI now, is:

1. Keep ACLI exactly as-is.
2. Standardize all future **real Codex CLI** usage on one Codex home/auth location.
